domains.title: The Place Where Heaven Descended
domains.subtitle: Myth, Gorge, and Sacred Rice
domains.lead: Takachiho is a town and gorge in the mountains of Kyūshū, famous as the place where Ninigi descended from heaven to begin the rule of the terrestrial world. Its name, 'High Thousand Ears of Grain,' evokes a landscape of tall rice and misty peaks where the divine once touched the earth.

cards.name: Heavenly Descent

mythology.lead: Takachiho's mythology centers on the descent of Ninigi and the performances that keep the cave myth alive.

myths.title: The Descent of Ninigi
myths.text: Amaterasu sent her grandson Ninigi to rule the earth, and he descended to Takachiho, where the peaks touched the clouds. From this base in Kyūshū, the imperial line would eventually move eastward to Yamato. Takachiho thus marks the starting point of Japan's sacred kingship.

myths.title: The Ama-no-Iwato Cave
myths.text: Takachiho is also associated with a cave where Amaterasu was said to have hidden. Local kagura performances reenact Uzume's dance and the return of the sun, keeping the myth alive in ritual and theater.

myths.title: Kagura in Takachiho
myths.text: The Yokagura of Takachiho are all-night performances of sacred dance that take place in villages during the winter. They preserve one of Japan's oldest living traditions of mythic reenactment.

lore.syncretism: Takachiho blends imperial mythology, local landscape, and folk performance. The descent of Ninigi gives it national significance, while the gorge and kagura give it local identity. It is a place where myth is not merely remembered but performed.
lore.culturalLegacy: Takachiho is a major tourist and pilgrimage destination, known for its gorge, waterfall, and winter kagura. It represents the mythic heart of Kyūshū and the point where the imperial narrative begins on earth.
lore.extendedMeditation: Takachiho is where story becomes landscape. The gorge, the waterfall, and the rice fields are not backdrops to the myth; they are the myth itself, still visible and still performed. To visit is to walk into the narrative.
lore.archaeology: Takachiho Gorge is a volcanic landscape formed by the eruption of Mount Aso, with basalt columns and the Manai Falls. The area preserves shrines and performance spaces associated with the descent myth and the local kagura tradition.
